Chapter 2: What It Means to Truly Follow
There comes a time in everyone’s life when you feel that unexpected call to change. Sometimes it sneaks up as a gentle nudge, other times it’s a lightning bolt—a realization that demands your attention. But the question behind it is always the same: Will you follow, even if it costs you something?
At first, it’s easy to say yes in your mind. But when you’re actually facing the moment—when you have to step out and leave your comfort zone—suddenly, things aren’t so simple.
Picture someone who’s always played it safe, sticking close to routines and familiar faces. Then, one day, they’re faced with a choice: maybe it’s speaking up for someone being treated unfairly, or giving up a comfort for someone else’s sake. The first instinct? Hesitation.
What if things go wrong? What if no one understands? The cost feels so immediate, so real.
And that’s really the core of discipleship—not just believing, but actually following.
It’s like standing at the base of a mountain. You can admire its beauty from afar, but climbing it? That’s a whole different story. The journey is unpredictable, and the trail isn’t always clear. There’ll be moments of doubt, fear, and even regret. But along the way, you start to feel something shift—a sense of purpose, a feeling that you’re finally living life with your whole heart.
Most folks think following means having all the answers, or at least a detailed map. But honestly? The call often comes with little explanation. You’re asked to take a step into the unknown, trusting that you’ll figure it out along the way.
I’m reminded of someone who left a steady job to serve in a place where help was desperately needed. Friends wondered why—pointing out all the risks, all the unknowns. But for this person, the call was unmistakable, even if the outcome wasn’t.
Obedience, then, isn’t about just following orders blindly. It’s about trust—trusting that the one who calls you actually knows the way, even when you can’t see what’s around the corner. It means letting go of the urge to control every detail, and being willing to trade comfort for something bigger.
Sure, there are sacrifices. You might have to let go of old habits. Relationships could change. Security is swapped for vulnerability. But with every step, something inside you changes. The person who once clung to safety discovers a new kind of freedom—a freedom that comes from living with real purpose and integrity.
The truth is, many people never take that step. They’re content just watching from the sidelines. But those who do—who really choose to follow—find that while the cost is real, it’s nothing compared to the joy of living a life that truly matters.
The journey might not be easy. But trust me, it’s worth every step.
